title: Mushroom, kale and butter bean hash with eggs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain kitchen staple: onion, mushrooms, garlic, tinned butter beans, kale, eggs, oil, paprika and thyme.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item on any Tesco shelf at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs one large lidded frying pan and simple frying and egg-cracking that a beginner can manage.

works.reason: 400g mushrooms, two tins of beans, 100g kale and four eggs make a sensible four-portion hash, with clear heats and timings and paprika, thyme and seasoning for flavour.

honest_times.reason: Slicing the onion, mushrooms and garlic and shredding the kale fits roughly 10 minutes, and the steps add up to about 15 minutes of cooking.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and fresh thyme is on the November list.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot, browned mushroom hash with kale suits a cold November morning, and the mushrooms lead the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Vegetables, pulses and eggs make a filling, balanced breakfast a family would happily eat again.
